failures.criterion: The merge gate's first step: the tester's evidence green at the head the reviewer will read, which includes the repository's CI at that head (skill://legion-worker/references/merge-gate.md). No CI verdict exists at this head and none can arrive while it stands.
failures.evidence: gh pr view 2571 --repo sjawhar/legion --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus -> {"mergeable":"CONFLICTING","mergeStateStatus":"DIRTY"}. gh api repos/sjawhar/legion/commits/<sha>/check-runs --jq .total_count answers 0 at the handoff head 6c48a4309c68af451853a5f016d7ed938a20bd7b, at the code head f5f24d9ba86d71e199a43ef27b43476b75528320 and at the forward-merge commit f4251949558b; gh run list --repo sjawhar/legion --branch legion/INFRA-338 lists no run at all. GitHub builds no merge ref for a conflicting head and so runs no required check on it. The conflict is main moving under the implementer's forward merge: main@origin is d7e1daaaaf7048e0519fe2d6750634376f7cee83, 9 commits past this branch's base 39b51494224f905493bf1c20e50be8b6f8fc024e, and git merge-tree --write-tree <main> <head> reports CONFLICT (content) in AGENTS.md, docs/kubernetes.md, scripts/e2e/README.md and skills/AGENTS.md (at the earlier main 772004c826be it was skills/AGENTS.md alone, so the set grows with every merge to main that touches this change's prose). Fix: the implementer brings main forward into the branch and pushes, which gives the head a merge ref and a CI run; the diff of the conflicted prose files changes, so the next testing round is a full one rather than a fingerprint re-check. Nothing of the change's own behaviour failed: every acceptance check below was green at this head, and the local stand-ins for the CI lanes were green too (bunx biome check . exit 0, 2 pre-existing warnings; bun run typecheck exit 0 in each of contracts, envoy-client, envoy-plugin, claude-envoy, pi-shared, pi-envoy, pi-legion, proof-editor, dispatch and docs/site; cd packages/daemon && go vet -tags e2e ./... exit 0; cd packages/daemon && go test ./... green but for internal/workspace, whose three failures -- TestGitWorktreeEntriesResolveACloneSymlinkOutsideTheWorkspace, TestProvisionRestoresALostGitWorktree and TestProvisionRestoresAWorkspaceWithNoRealParentCommit -- fail identically in a git archive extract of the merge base 39b51494224f, so they are this pod's environment and not this change). Those local runs are not CI and are not evidence for the merge gate; CI at the merged head is.

failures.criterion: A2, first two sentences: 'A test starts deep-worker from a role session, and the task call returns before the subagent ends. A message sent to the role while the subagent runs is in the role's context at its next model turn, within 30 seconds of the message's arrival.' No test in this change does either.
failures.evidence: The change delivers A2's third sentence alone: packages/pi-legion/src/shipped-agents.test.ts gains the case '%s declares no blocking field' over agents/, and the implementer's own A2 proof entry names that file as its whole surface ('the agent files the plugin ships, read as Oh My Pi reads them'). No test starts a role session and dispatches deep-worker: grep over packages/pi-legion, packages/pi-shared and packages/pi-envoy for a case driving a task subagent finds none, packages/pi-legion/extensions/legion-phase-stall-omp.test.ts's ten cases cover the reminder and its last case a background *bash* job, and no case anywhere measures a message's arrival against the next model turn. Neither of the plan's two specDepartures covers A2 (they are A3's claude-backend-tmux.sh run and A4's ci-red-takeover run), so this is an undelivered acceptance criterion rather than an accepted departure. The behaviour itself holds -- I drove it on the real pinned binary (/opt/omp/bin/omp, the build .omp-pin names) in a session with Legion's configuration, through packages/pi-shared/test/omp-harness.ts's spawnRpc with the packages/pi-legion package root as the loaded extension so agents/ is discovered, a stand-in gateway, and the parent prompted to hand the work to one deep-worker: the task tool_result read 'Spawned agent `DeterminedStoat` ...', the parent's agent_end came at 7.84 s while the subagent's own model request was still held, the stand-in released that request at 27.91 s, and the job's completion woke the session into a fresh turn at 27.96 s carrying the async-result system notice. So what is missing is the regression lock and the acceptance test, not the behaviour. Two things cost time in building that probe and belong in the test: deep-worker declares model: ["@deep"], a role writeStandinProfile does not map, so without an extra modelRoles line ('  deep: standin/standin-model' passed as its config argument) the subagent dies in 476 ms with 'Error: No model selected' while the parent still reports the job completed -- a false green for any case that only checks the parent; and the subagent's own Messages request is told from the parent's by deep-worker's system prompt ('You are an autonomous coding worker'), not by request order, since the host also sends label and self-check side requests. The second sentence needs a message the session really receives: packages/pi-envoy/extensions/card-delivery-omp.test.ts shows the shape (LEGION_TEST_NATS_URL, a NATS publish on notifications.agent.<session id>), and the measurement is the delivery's arrival stamp against the next Messages request.
